newsitem.title: USA: CEM Corp sees fiscal 1997 lower than 1996.
newsitem.headline: CEM Corp sees fiscal 1997 lower than 1996.

text.p: CEM Corp said it expects fiscal 1997 earnings to be "substantially lower" than a year ago.
For the 1996 fiscal year, the company earned $2.9 million or $0.78 on net sales of $31.5 million.
Earlier the company reported first quarter net income of $106,000, or $0.03 per share, down from $677,000, or $0.18 per share in the year ago period.
The company said it was continuing to see "softness in shipments for government and environmental applications in the United States."
CEM also said the international portion of its business was sluggish, especially in Europe.

"Although we expect some recovery in subsequent periods due to seasonal factors, earnings for fiscal 1997 as a whole are expected to be substantially lower than a year ago. We are confident that this outlook represents only a temporary break in CEM's long-term record of growth," Michael J. Collins, president and chief Executive officer said.
He said the company's newest product, the Star System, was introduced in March and continues to be well received.
CEM manufactures microwave-based instruments for testing and process control.
